risks: Low to moderate: remote titration could over-treat or miss a severe reading outside hub hours; usual care continues in both arms and severe readings have an escalation route.
consent: Written informed consent on the postnatal ward before discharge, with interpreters and translated information; women can stop monitoring at any time and keep their usual care.
data: Readings are held on the app provider's platform under a data processing agreement and in the hub record; the analysis file uses study numbers.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: women without a smartphone, women needing an interpreter, younger mothers, recent migrants and women in deprived areas are the most likely to be excluded or to report less. Loan phones, paper diaries with hub calls and interpreter calls are part of the intervention, and outcomes are reported by digital access and language.
effectiveness: The trial is useful if it shows whether remote monitoring improves six-week control within the unit's own service and reaches women equally.
efficiency: Uses existing midwives and charity-funded devices; no extra clinic visits.
costs: Monitors, app licence and loan phones funded by the charity; hub midwife time within existing roles.
grants: None beyond the charity award; a positive result could support a larger trial powered for readmission.
partnerships: The midwife hub, community midwives, family doctors, the maternity assessment unit and a maternity voices group.
rebPath: Research ethics application to be submitted, following ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki; no allocation before approval.
limitations: Surrogate primary outcome; unblinded; underpowered for readmission.
summary: Written consent with interpreters, an escalation route, and inclusive delivery reported by digital access and language.
